## Reading in Data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
steel.industry <- read.csv("Resampled_SIPD.csv")

head(steel.industry)
```

## Testing-training split

```{r}
# Getting rid of bad columns
drop <- c("X", "index", "date", "Day_of_week")
steel.industry <- steel.industry[, !(names(steel.industry) %in% drop)]

# Indicator variables
steel.industry$Load_Type <- factor(
  steel.industry$Load_Type,
  levels = c("Light_Load", "Medium_Load", "Maximum_Load")
  )
steel.industry$WeekStatus <- factor(steel.industry$WeekStatus)

# Training-testing split
set.seed(42)
train_ind <- sample(
  seq_len(nrow(steel.industry)),
  size = floor(0.80 * nrow(steel.industry))
  )

trainData <- steel.industry[train_ind, ]
testData <- steel.industry[-train_ind, ]
```

## Summaries of numeric variables

```{r}
num.true.vect <- sapply(trainData, is.numeric)
num <- trainData[num.true.vect]
summary(num)
```

## Summaries of categorical variables

```{r}
categoric <- lapply(trainData[!num.true.vect], factor)
lapply(categoric[names(categoric) != "date"], table)
```

## Multivariate relationships
```{r}
pairs(num)

library(car)
# Building a full model with numeric predictors
full.mod <- lm(Usage_kWh ~ ., data = steel.industry)

vif(full.mod)
```

```{r}
response <- steel.industry$Usage_kWh
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
boxplot(Usage_kWh ~ Load_Type,  data = steel.industry, ylab = "Usage (kWh)",
        main = "(a) By load type", xlab = "")
boxplot(Usage_kWh ~ WeekStatus, data = steel.industry, ylab = "Usage (kWh)",
        main = "(b) By week status", xlab = "")
```
